mutations.because: The whole lane is the element's override reaching BOTH renderers identically (HL-D5, HL-D8). Reverting the text case to the brief-level font reopens exactly the gap HL5f closed for tone: an element asking for 400/Lora would ship markup that lies about its own raster fallback — the canvas would draw the override and the ad would not — and nothing else in the pipeline compares the two, because the markup is never rasterised (D122).

HL-D8 admits the override to exactly the two kinds whose rendering reads it, and the field table — not a branch — is what refuses it elsewhere (the HL1 mechanism). Add style to image's allowed row and an image element starts carrying a font no renderer reads: a field accepted at both boundaries and honoured by neither, the D134 unread-field shape this table exists to prevent.

The HL5e element style reaches the assembled bytes through htmlElementFont, so the memo key must weigh it (Qodo finding, fix round). Drop the two style slots and a style-only edit is a cache hit on the previous reading: the meter and the over-budget warning report bytes the generation path will never produce, and the whole lane's promise — the figure the editor shows is the unit's real weight — silently breaks behind the single-entry cache.
